solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Round we had — and hadn't paid

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
we had shortens to we'd, spelt here without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a round of drinks they ordered but skipped out on paying for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a round of drinks, but it is the letter O. WE'D (we had) follows it, without the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still owed is a debt that has not yet been settled, so it hadn't been paid.

clue.text: Fully extended providing picnic?

definitions.meaning: stretched or opened out wide, like wings
putting out a spread of food, as on a picnic blanket outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into OUT SPREAD: a spread of food laid out, as at a picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread out wide describes something stretched to its fullest extent.

clue.text: Satanist's lived riotously — wish proper reforming's to come

definitions.note: read as Satanist is, so the definition is the noun Satanist

indicators.note: to come means the second piece follows the first
acting riotously means wildly, so the letters of lived are thrown into a new order
reforming means reshaping, so the letters of wish proper are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A Satanist has lived wildly but wishes to reform into a proper person in future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satanist's' reads as 'Satanist is', and 'reforming's to come' as 'reforming is to follow', so the second anagram comes after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A Satanist is one who venerates the Devil, a worshipper of Satan.

clue.text: Very useful, home price covering rebuilt lab

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: the word for price goes around the other piece like a cover

parts.note: a thing's value is its price

indicators.note: the letters of lab are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: An estate agent praises a house whose price includes a newly refurbished laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' is the crossword convention that being in means being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond price in its worth is extremely helpful, the everyday sense of this word.

clue.text: Second of this month

definitions.meaning: a moment, a very short time
an old commercial-letter term for a date in the current month, as in your letter of the 5th inst.

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is old business correspondence: 'the 10th instant' meant the tenth of the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief moment is a second; in old letters the word marked a date in the current month.

clue.text: Envoy, a German taking part as tourist

indicators.note: the answer takes part of the letters of the words Envoy, a German

explanation.surface: An ambassador and a German take part as tourists on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across EnVOY A GERman.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyager is a traveller on a journey, and so a kind of tourist.

clue.text: Cricketer and members going over feature

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means placed on top of the next piece

parts.note: legs are limbs, also called members
the lip is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A cricketer and fellow club members go over the main feature of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg slip is a close fielding position behind the batter on the leg side, so the word also names the fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: This names a fielding position in cricket and so also the fielder who stands there.

clue.text: Final cardiogram disguised bloomer

indicators.note: disguised means the letters of final cardiogram are rearranged to hide them

explanation.surface: A last heart trace was disguised to hide a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder or a loaf; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange-flowered garden plant is something that blooms, hence a bloomer.

clue.text: Wield cross held in upturned palm perhaps

indicators.note: the cross is held inside the overturned tree
upturned in a down clue means the word for a palm is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a palm is an example of a tree
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: Someone holds a cross in an upturned palm to exert power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'palm' looks like a hand, but it is a palm TREE; 'upturned' makes EERT and X is 'held in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert influence or force is to bring it to bear, to wield it.

clue.text: Mockery made of tryst Eva organised

indicators.note: the letters of tryst and Eva are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: A secret lovers' meeting arranged by a woman called Eva turned into a farce.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque imitation or parody is a mockery of the real thing.

clue.text: Awkward ridge gets left in waistbelt

indicators.note: the letter for left sits inside the rearranged ridge
awkward means clumsily arranged, so the letters of ridge are rearranged

explanation.surface: An uncomfortable bump in the fabric is found in someone's belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' makes GIRDE from RIDGE; L goes 'in' it before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle is a belt or sash worn around the middle of the body.

clue.text: Two Spanish articles following pop as a local speciality

indicators.note: the two articles come after the word for pop

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, as is pa
el is a Spanish word for the
la is the feminine Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Two Spanish newspaper pieces about pop music being a regional thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces, but it means the grammatical articles EL and LA.
explanation.definitionFit: This rice dish is the famous regional dish of Valencia in Spain.

clue.text: Green buggy?

parts.note: a green is a golf course, and a buggy is a small vehicle, here one driven around a golf course

explanation.definitionFit: Golfers ride in a small electric vehicle around the course and its greens.

clue.text: Grain port

definitions.meaning: a cereal plant used for bread and whisky
A town in East Sussex, England, one of the old Cinque Ports on the coast

explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal grass and also a historic English harbour town.

clue.text: Train rodents to roll over after French bread

indicators.note: the reversed rodents come after the French money

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and the currency of France is the euro

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word for rodents back to front

parts.note: rats are rodents

explanation.surface: Someone tries to teach mice and rats to roll over, tempting them with a baguette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French bread' looks like a baguette; bread is slang for money, the EURO. 'to roll over' turns RATS into STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The high-speed passenger rail service through the Channel Tunnel is a train.

clue.text: Wrote from prison: 'Study's gone west'

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure, informally a prison

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: A prisoner writes a letter home saying their study room has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone west' usually means died; here it reverses DEN to NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen a letter is to write it, so the past tense means wrote.

clue.text: No-holds-barred cannibalism?

definitions.meaning: a dog eating another dog is animal cannibalism, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally the phrase describes one dog eating another: canine cannibalism.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-throat, ruthlessly competitive struggle has no holds barred.

clue.text: Young woman's mother the French brought back

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

indicators.note: brought back means the French article is reversed

parts.note: les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: A young woman's mother brought back French people with her.
explanation.walkthrough: A dam is a farming term for an animal's mother, usually a mare or ewe.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel is an old-fashioned or literary word for a young unmarried woman, a maiden.

clue.text: Pronounce as an alternative to wonder

indicators.note: pronounce means the word is said aloud and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to pronounce a word as an alternative way of expressing wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, OR and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is a feeling of reverent wonder or amazement.

clue.text: Fat left a stain finally on jazzy lino

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of stain
jazzy means lively and vivid, so the letters of lino are jumbled

explanation.surface: Grease left a stain on a brightly patterned linoleum floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link meaning the jumbled lino is placed after the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This greasy substance from sheep's wool is a kind of fat used in ointments.

clue.text: Unbecoming to be in drag, if getting a makeover

indicators.note: a makeover changes appearance, so the letters of in drag and if are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if dressing in drag is undignified, especially with a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin infra dignitatem, it means beneath one's dignity, unseemly.

clue.text: Learned not to start or repeat

indicators.note: not to start means the first letter of the word for learned is removed

parts.note: literate means educated, learned

explanation.surface: A learned person is told not to begin or to repeat themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to start' takes the L off LITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, a synonym of repeat.

clue.text: Footballers agree with a deadly final ending?

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, the body governing English football
tally means agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Footballers agree that a cup final might end in sudden death.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adverb: done in a way that ends in death.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ends this way when it results in death, a deadly outcome.

clue.text: Journalist's taken back intended hostile challenge

indicators.note: taken back means the abbreviation for the journalist is reversed

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
one's intended is one's fiance, the person one is engaged to

explanation.surface: A journalist's betrothed partner is taken aback by a hostile challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' looks like a verb meaning planned; it is a noun for a betrothed partner, FIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Open resistance or a bold refusal to obey amounts to a hostile challenge.

clue.text: Setter perhaps needs clue at the end to cover up dead duck

indicators.note: the dog and final letter go around, covering, the abbreviation for dead

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, an example

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of clue

explanation.surface: A crossword setter adds a final clue to cover up a dead duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler, but it is a dog; DOG plus E covers D.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or blow is to evade it, to dodge it.

clue.text: Journey cut short through irrelevancies

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word for journey is dropped

parts.note: a trip is a journey
via means through or by way of

explanation.surface: A journey is cut short because of trivial distractions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the P off TRIP, giving TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial details or facts of little importance are irrelevancies.

clue.text: I sped round lake to drive away

indicators.note: turned round means the letters of I sped are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A driver says they sped around a lake in order to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the route around the lake, but it rearranges I SPED into DISPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel fears or doubts is to drive them away or scatter them.

clue.text: Many-sided but with no sides?

definitions.meaning: something perfectly circular has no sides at all, as with a circle

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: completely circular, with no straight sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile in many skills is the usual sense; read as two words, it describes a perfect circle.

clue.text: Fry often gets tipsy around the Queen — sheer impudence!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for the Queen
getting tipsy means becoming unsteady, so the letters of Fry and often are rearranged

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone named Fry often gets drunk in front of the Queen, which is outrageously cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives EFFRONTY, and the royal cipher goes inside it before the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameless boldness or insolent cheek is sheer impudence.

clue.text: Monster not on trail

indicators.note: not means the clue word on is taken out

parts.note: a dragon is a mythical monster

explanation.surface: A monster is not following the trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' removes ON from DRAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something is to haul it along behind, the sense of to trail.
